description.narrative:
Stakeholder effects - Improved access to finance for social sector, specifically to disadvantaged groups in rural areas: The proposed investment is expected to support Chongho Bridges lending to targeted groups of population that are eligible under ICMA Social Bond Framework, including but not limited to women, people living below the poverty line, and other vulnerable groups as defined by the framework. The proposed investment in the social bond to be issued by Chongho Bridge aims to bridge the financing gap of those social sectors, especially in rural areas of China.
Market Creation: Sustainability: Following IFCs first anchor investment in a social bond issued by Haier Financial Leasing in 2022, the proposed investment represents IFCs second investment in a social bond, which aims to replicate IFCs successful experience in Haier Financial Leasing project. These investments form part of a systematic intervention by IFC to create a credible and sustainable market for social bonds by Chinese institutions. With more successful replication and roll out of social bond programs in China, IFC anticipates that the issuance of an ICMA-compliant social bond by a private financial institution will enable other players in the market to follow suit with internationally recolonized instruments and to bridge the financing gap of social projects.

The proposed project entails IFC investment of up to US$75 million equivalent in local currency in the Social Bond to be issued by Chongho Bridge Management Limited (Chongho Bridge, or the Company, and formerly known as CD Finance or CFPA MF), a long-standing partner of IFC for more than a decade. The Company engages in microfinance business through its micro credit company subsidiaries and is the largest rural focused microfinance provider in China. IFC will play an anchor investor role in the social bond placement to help catalyze mobilization from other investors.
